Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a bespoke 180-day transient residency in Redwood Private; and we can implement an emergency rollback window for recently deleted objects with a defined runbook.

High-level options we typically offer (to be captured in the order form):
- Option A: 180-day ephemeral residency, automated purge after 180 days, standard certificate of deletion (log + SHA256 digest).
- Option B: 180-day residency + 48-hour soft-rollback retention (deleted objects retained in encrypted append-only escrow for 48 hours post-delete); forensic export on demand (48-hr SLA for retrieval).
- Option C: 180-day residency + 90-day escrow for high-sensitivity datasets (extra fee).

I've attached an initial draft order form and a short playbook for forensic hold procedures. Marcus can add a technical note on how the rollback pipeline works and the limits on restore granularity (per request vs per-tenant).

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to confirm technical feasibility and expected timeline for plumbing escrow hooks into the deletion pipeline.
- We send a redline of the SLA appendix with the chosen option.
- Legal teams to align on language for "certificate of deletion" and evidence delivery.

I'll leave rest to Marcus and Lauren — thanks for looping us in.

Best,

Rajiv / Stephanie —

Technical note on the rollback/escrow approach we discussed:

How it works (summary):
- Deletion flow: when a record hits its retention expiry we run a deterministic purge job that removes KV entries and metadata.
- Soft-rollback escrow: before the final destruction step we store an encrypted, tenant-scoped snapshot (metadata + minimal payload pointers) in a hardened, access-controlled escrow bucket for 48 hours. The escrow stores ciphertext plus a deletion manifest (timestamp, object digests).
- Restore granularity: restores are at the object-key level (not ad-hoc single-token rehydration). We can provide on-demand exports (JSONL) for forensics.

Constraints / SLAs:
- For Option B (48-hour escrow) we can commit to a 48-hour retrieval SLA for restores during the escrow window. Restoration for objects outside the escrow window is not possible unless Option C escrow is chosen.
- Proof-of-deletion: we can provide a signed certificate containing deletion manifest, SHA256 digests, and job run IDs. Archival logs (immutable) are available for audit for 12 months.
- Forensic hold: we support a hold flag that prevents purge; this will pause automated purges for the flagged dataset but may incur storage/retention fees. Holds must be requested via the portal + signed request.

Operational notes:
- We need to confirm whether NovaPulse requires per-object chain-of-custody metadata (we support it but turn it on per dataset).
- Escrow increases storage costs and has a small effect on Redis/KV cache eviction behavior; estimated cost impact for a mid-size dataset (~50M tokens/month) is ~3-5% additional monthly unit costs.

I'll work with SRE to estimate cost numbers for the order form.

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus — couple clarifying items:

1) Chain-of-custody: yes, we need per-object chain-of-custody for PII flagged payloads (stored as metadata) for regulatory audits.
2) Certificate content: the cert should include object digest, deletion manifest ID, job run ID, timestamp, and the signing key thumbprint.
3) Can you confirm whether the escrow snapshots are stored in a FIPS-compliant vault/KMS? Our security team requires FIPS-validated KMS for escrow encryption keys.

If you can confirm those three, we'll run this by legal and tell you which option they prefer.

Rajiv

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency window + emergency rollback question

Rajiv —

Short answers to your clarifications:
- Chain-of-custody: supported. We emit per-object metadata with an immutable append-only audit id (AOID) that surfaces in the deletion manifest and the certificate. We can enable this for PII-flagged datasets at provisioning.
- Certificate contents: we'll include SHA256 digest, deletion_manifest_id, job_run_id, timestamp, and the KMS key thumbprint. Certificate will be signed with our platform key and we can provide the public thumbprint for verification.
- KMS: escrow snapshots are encrypted with a customer-configurable KMS; for Private deployments we support FIPS 140-2 validated HSM-backed keys (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) — we'll note the selected KMS in the order form.

Operational proposal to include in SLA appendix: 
- Agreed baseline: 180-day transient residency + 48-hour escrow for deleted objects (Option B).
- Forensic retrieval: 48-hour SLA for restores during escrow window, export as JSONL with AOID and chain-of-custody metadata.
- Certificate: provided within 4 business days of deletion (signed PDF + machine-readable manifest).
- Holds: legal/forensic holds require signed request and pause automated purge; charged per GB-month.

If that lineup looks OK I'll generate a redline for the order form and send to your legal team.

—Priyom
